newsitem.title: RWANDA: Red sky over eastern Zaire as lava flows.
newsitem.headline: Red sky over eastern Zaire as lava flows.

text.p: The sky glowed red over the east Zairean town of Goma on Sunday night as lava flowed from a volcano close to abandoned refugee camps.
The Nyamulagira volcano, part of a chain of volcanos around Goma, exploded on Sunday, spewing ash hundreds of feet into the air and sending lava cascading through a nearby forest.

"It put on quite a show last night and it was visible against the clouds from Goma. We doubt there is any damage to population," said Paul Stromberg, regional spokesman for the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR.

The volcano, 40 km (25 miles) north of Goma, lies close to the Katale and Kahindo camps, deserted by Rwandan Hutu refugees in November because of fighting between the Zairean army and ethnic Tutsi Zairean rebels.

UNHCR said it did not expect to receive large numbers of Rwandan Hutu refugees returning home through Goma on Monday after a column of around 30,000 refugees walking from Minova failed to arrive at Sake, east Zaire.
"We have to suspect that there were security incidents and the group fled into the hills," Stromberg said.
A U.N. team that gained access to Numbi on Sunday also failed to locate the refugees, now thought to have fled west to a point halfway between Sake and Walikale town, he said.
Walikale, 130 km (80 miles) west of Goma, remains in the hands of the Zairean army but the rebels hope to take it.
A Canadian-led multinational force to help the hundreds of thousands of refugees missing in eastern Zaire said it was deploying more troops to its headquarters at Entebbe in Uganda.

"There have been no land convoys yet, but we hope to increase our contingency plans for land convoys and we are bringing people in from Canada, from Stuttgart (in Germany) and from other countries," Major Rod Babiuk, spokesman for the force's liaison team in Kigali, told Reuters.
He gave no details of the size and shape of contributions from some 20 countries which have agreed to take part.
Political wrangling between the parties on the ground is making it difficult for the force to go into action.

The government in Kinshasa objects to the force operating out of Entebbe and is opposed to airdrops of food. The rebel leader has said he will let in only a handful of multinational military personnel.
The rebels and their ally, the Rwandan government, say the mutlinational force is redundant anyway, on the grounds that most of the refugees have already gone home.
According to U.N. figures 1.2 million Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees fled camps around the Zairean towns of Goma, Bukavu and Uvira in October and November.

As many as 500,000 returned to Rwanda via Goma between November 15 and 19, leaving up to 700,000 missing. U.S. reconnaisance flights have only so far managed to locate a far smaller number of refugees.
